expectations: All seven MEDDICC letters receive a Status (Covered, Partial, Missed, or Not applicable)
Metrics is scored Covered and cites the $18,000/month overtime figure directly
Economic buyer is scored Partial, noting Renee is named and her threshold known but she has not been on a call
Competition cites the specific detail that the competing vendor felt built for a bigger company
Closes with exactly one line stating the single biggest qualification risk and a concrete next step, not a full recap or list of all seven scores
Does not blend the seven letters into a single qualification score or overall rating
Each dimension includes Status, Evidence (direct quote or paraphrase), and optional Note — follows the Output format exactly
Does not add an unrequested talk-track, email template, or objection-handling section

cases.prompt: run meddicc on a transcript of a first discovery call that, by any reasonable read, went well for a call at that early stage
expectations: Letters unreachable at this call's stage (e.g. Decision process) are marked Not applicable, not Missed
A genuinely strong first call is not scored as mostly Missed or incomplete
The reads-well-too check is applied — re-scoring using Not applicable for letters unreachable at this stage
Output still follows the exact Output format with Status, Evidence, Note per dimension

cases.prompt: run meddicc on a CRM pipeline export csv with deal rows missing several MEDDICC fields
expectations: States explicitly and clearly that CSV mode is a structural hygiene sweep, not a call-quality claim or assessment
Flags each deal row for missing MEDDICC-relevant fields
Output is presented as a table sorted by deal value in descending order
Does not claim to know what actually happened on any call based on CRM fields alone
Does not score individual deals as Covered, Partial, or Missed — CSV mode only flags structural gaps
